item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Craig folded a piece of paper in half and cut out a shape.

[Image: Folded paper with cut-out shape]

Draw a picture to show what the cut-out shape will look like when it is opened up and flattened out.

descriptors: The drawing of the cut-out shape corresponds to figure A.
The drawing of the remaining piece of paper corresponds to figure B.
Other correct.
Drawing corresponds to figure C.
Drawing corresponds to figure D.
Drawings correspond to figures E or F or G.
Other incorrect.

item.scoring_notes: Note: See the examples above. The accuracy in drawing is not important, nor is the size of the figure.
item.figure_description: A vertical rectangular outline representing a piece of paper folded in half vertically. The vertical left edge is labeled with an arrow pointing to it and the word "fold". Along this folded edge, a cut-out profile is drawn: starting from a point on the left edge, a straight line segment angles up and right, turns back down and to the left to form a sharp inward notch, then curves outward to the right in a rounded semicircle, and finally curves back down and to the left to meet the folded edge at the bottom.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Jay has to draw a shape.
- It must have 5 sides.
- It must have one line of symmetry.
Jay has started to draw the shape.
Complete Jay’s shape.

[Image: an incomplete shape with three sides forming a rectangle on a grid.]

descriptors:
Correct shape drawn which has 5 sides and 1 line of symmetry. The new vertex must be within ±2 mm of the line of symmetry (accept the new vertex anywhere on the line of symmetry, provided there are 5 sides).
[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. Two lines drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.] OR
[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. Two lines sloping inwards are drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.]

[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. The rectangle is completed with a fourth line and then two additional lines are drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.]
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: A 10 by 10 square grid. A three-sided incomplete shape is drawn with thick black lines along the grid lines: a horizontal bottom segment 6 units long (leaving 2 units of margin on the left and 2 units on the right along the bottom edge of the grid), and two vertical segments each 4 units tall rising upward from the two ends of the bottom segment (leaving 6 units of grid space above them). The top of the shape is open.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In the picture there are a number of geometric shapes, like circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles. For example, the sun looks like a circle.

Draw lines to three other different objects in the picture and write what shapes they look like.

[Image: A house and yard scene with geometric objects]

descriptors: Any three of square, rectangle, triangle, trapezoid, diamond/rhombus, kite correctly identified
Any two of the above plus circle
Any two of the above correctly identified
Any one of the above plus circle
Incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
A line drawing of a scene containing geometric elements:
- In the upper right sky, a circular shape is labeled "sun" with a line drawn to the label "circle".
- Behind the house are trees rendered with leafy texture.
- In the center is a two-story house:
  - The roof features two dormers, each topped with a triangular roof and containing a rectangular window divided into four square panes.
  - A small chimney is on the roof ridge.
  - The main facade is rectangular, featuring two rectangular windows (each divided into four panes) and a central rectangular front door.
  - The door contains a diamond-shaped (rhombus) window and a small round doorknob.
- In front of the door is a stone path composed of trapezoidal and triangular paving stones.
- To the lower left of the house stands a lamppost consisting of a circular light mounted on a tall, narrow rectangular post set in grass.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Jill had a rectangular piece of paper.

[Image: A rectangle divided horizontally into two equal halves by a dotted line]

She cut her paper along the dotted line and made an L shape like this.

[Image: An L-shaped figure made of two rectangular strips]

Which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The area of the L shape is greater than the area of the rectangle.

options.label: B
options.text: The area of the L shape is equal to the area of the rectangle.

options.label: C
options.text: The area of the L shape is less than the area of the rectangle.

options.label: D
options.text: You cannot work out which area is greater without measuring.

reference_items.figure_description:
The first figure shows a horizontal rectangle with a dashed horizontal line dividing it into two equal top and bottom halves.

The second figure shows an L shape made from the two halves: one vertical rectangular strip on the left and one horizontal rectangular strip at the bottom right, joined along part of their edges at a right angle.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:
An 8 by 8 grid of square cells with a vertical dashed line of symmetry running along the central vertical grid line (between the 4th and 5th columns from the left).
To the right of the dashed line is a six-sided polygon with vertices at grid intersections (with column lines 0 to 8 from left to right, and row lines 0 to 8 from top to bottom):
- (column 4, row 3) on the dashed line
- (column 5, row 2)
- (column 6, row 4)
- (column 7, row 4)
- (column 7, row 6)
- (column 4, row 5) on the dashed line

The edges of the polygon connect these vertices in sequence:
- A straight segment from (4, 3) up and right to (5, 2)
- A segment from (5, 2) down and right to (6, 4)
- A horizontal segment from (6, 4) to (7, 4)
- A vertical segment from (7, 4) down to (7, 6)
- A slanted segment from (7, 6) up and left to (4, 5)
- A vertical segment of length 2 along the dashed line from (4, 5) up to (4, 3)

reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

C.

USE: 2 Trapezoid Tiles
MAKE: A 6-sided figure that is not the same shape as the one you made in Part B
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors: Any of four figures (6-sided) that was not used in part B.
Repeats a correct figure already given in part B
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part C response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.

reference_items.figure_description:
A square grid 6 units wide and 6 units tall. A vertical dashed line labeled "m" at the bottom divides the grid vertically down the center (3 units from the left edge and 3 units from the right edge). On the left side of line m, a right triangle is drawn along the grid lines with vertices at:
- 2 units from the left edge and 2 units above the bottom edge (the right-angled vertex, located 1 unit to the left of line m)
- 1 unit from the left edge and 2 units above the bottom edge (located 2 units to the left of line m)
- 2 units from the left edge and 5 units above the bottom edge (1 unit below the top edge, located 1 unit to the left of line m).
The vertical leg of the triangle is 3 units long and lies along the grid line 1 unit to the left of line m; the horizontal base is 1 unit long and lies 2 units above the bottom edge.

reference_items.figure_description: A quadrilateral kite shape oriented diagonally on a blank background. It has a sharp, acute vertex pointing toward the bottom left. From this vertex, two long straight sides of equal length extend upward and to the right: one side goes steeply up and right to an upper vertex, and the other side goes gently up and right to a lower-right vertex. The top side is a short horizontal segment extending rightward from the upper vertex, and the right side is a short vertical segment extending upward from the lower-right vertex, meeting at a top-right corner.

[Image: 3-D figure]

Which of these could be folded to make a shape like the 3-D figure above?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a perspective drawing of a right triangular prism lying horizontally on one rectangular face. The front and back faces are triangles, connected by three rectangular faces.

Below are four candidate nets labeled A, B, C, and D:
- A: A chain consisting of a rectangle at an angle, a triangle, a central horizontal rectangle, a triangle, and another rectangle angled upward.
- B: Three identical horizontal rectangles stacked vertically, with two triangles attached to the right edge of the top two rectangles, pointing to the right.
- C: Two horizontal rectangles stacked vertically with two triangles attached to their left side pointing left, and a third rectangle extending to the right with a triangle attached at its right end.
- D: Three identical horizontal rectangles stacked vertically in a column; one triangle is attached to the right side of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle is attached to the left side of the bottom rectangle pointing left.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
